summary: The sensors-mcu-meta-hal group has 263 rows: 259 regular files and 4 symlinks, spread over odm_a (43), product_a (19), system_a (67), system_ext_a (123) and vendor_a (11). Its core is the vendor sensors HAL: an odm-partition HIDL service (vendor.oculus.hardware.sensors@1.0-service) built on vendor.oculus.hardware.sensors@1.0.so. It reads a TOML config at /vendor/etc/sensorservice.cfg and is selected at boot by persist.vendor.oculus.sensor.service.impl, which odm_a/etc/build.prop sets to sensorservice. Alternative implementations sit beside it: a mock HAL (disabled, no boot trigger), sensoremu and sensor-emulator, plus flicker and IAD HAL services. The framework side is the system-partition sensorservice daemon with libsensorservice.so and android.hardware.sensors 1.0/2.0/2.1 client libraries, and sensorproxy runs from system_ext. Adjacent HALs in the same classification are the sensorlock AIDL HAL, catty, dock, telemetry and devicecert, along with feature and privileged-permission XML. The group also contains TorchScript IMU-only tracker archives, PyTorch Lite microgesture archives, and the odm keylayout and keychar for oculus-device. Paths in evidence are relative to the read-only mount root <image>/mnt.

claims.claim: The sensorservice.cfg file is TOML with top-level nice_constellation = "ruby", [imu.default_rate] fallback = 800 and [mag.default_rate] fallback = 25. Comments say the device-specific keys must match kDeviceVersionName in libdeviceid. The same nice_constellation line appears in mrsystemservice.cfg and trackingservice.cfg.
claims.label: verified
claims.evidence: command: cat vendor_a/etc/sensorservice.cfg. output: nice_constellation = "ruby" / [imu.default_rate] / fallback = 800 / [mag.default_rate] / fallback = 25 / comment: NOTE: these keys must exactly match the strings in kDeviceVersionName in libdeviceid. command: grep -rl -a nice_constellation (on mnt). output includes system_a/system/etc/mrsystemservice.cfg and system_a/system/etc/trackingservice.cfg.

claims.claim: Init starts the sensors HAL only when the property selects it. The service vendor.oculus.sensors-hal-1-0 runs at class hal as user system, group system camera, declares interface vendor.oculus.hardware.sensors@1.0::IExternalTimingProvider default, uses task_profiles sensorServicePolicy and is marked disabled. It starts on boot when persist.vendor.oculus.sensor.service.impl=sensorservice. The sensoremu and sensor-emulator services use the same property with values sensoremu and sensor-emulator. odm_a/etc/build.prop sets sensorservice.
claims.label: verified
claims.evidence: command: cat odm_a/etc/init/vendor.oculus.hardware.sensors@1.0-service-debug.rc. output (excerpt): service vendor.oculus.sensors-hal-1-0 /odm/bin/hw/vendor.oculus.hardware.sensors@1.0-service / interface vendor.oculus.hardware.sensors@1.0::IExternalTimingProvider default / class hal / user system / group system camera / task_profiles sensorServicePolicy / disabled / on boot && property:persist.vendor.oculus.sensor.service.impl=sensorservice / start vendor.oculus.sensors-hal-1-0. command: sed -n '44,49p' odm_a/etc/build.prop. output: line 47 persist.vendor.oculus.sensor.service.impl=sensorservice. command: grep -rn 'persist.vendor.oculus.sensor.service.impl' mnt. output: odm.sensoremu.rc:13 (=sensoremu), odm.sensor-emulator.rc:13 (=sensor-emulator), debug rc:18 (=sensorservice).
claims.reason: Confirmed: service block (class hal, user system, group system camera, SYS_NICE, task_profiles sensorServicePolicy, interface IExternalTimingProvider default, disabled); on-boot trigger gated on persist.vendor.oculus.sensor.service.impl=sensorservice; build.prop line 47 sets sensorservice; sensoremu and sensor-emulator gates use sensoremu and sensor-emulator. Not accurate: 'only when the property selects it'. system_ext_a/bin/virtualcontroller_ctl sets kSensorSvcName=vendor.oculus.sensors-hal-1-0 and runs start $sensorSvcNew and stop for the old service. odm_a/bin/syncboss_consumers_ctl lists the service in SERVICES and runs start, stop and restart on it, so init starts it at runtime outside the boot trigger.
claims.corrected_claim: The debug init file defines vendor.oculus.sensors-hal-1-0 (class hal, user system, group system camera, capabilities SYS_NICE, task_profiles sensorServicePolicy, interface vendor.oculus.hardware.sensors@1.0::IExternalTimingProvider default, disabled). Its only boot trigger starts it when persist.vendor.oculus.sensor.service.impl=sensorservice, which odm_a/etc/build.prop line 47 sets. The sensoremu and sensor-emulator services use the same property with the values sensoremu and sensor-emulator. The service is also started and stopped at runtime by name from the shell scripts virtualcontroller_ctl (system_ext_a/bin) and syncboss_consumers_ctl (odm_a/bin).

claims.claim: The sensor emulator is provided by two init services. Service vendor.sensoremu (/odm/bin/sensoremu) runs as root and is oneshot and disabled. Service vendor.sensor-emulator (/odm/bin/sensor-emulator) is the same shape. Both have on-boot triggers gated on the sensor impl property. SELinux maps both binaries to hal_oculus_sensors_default_exec, and their data directories /data/vendor/misc/sensoremu and /data/vendor/misc/sensor-emulator to sensoremu_odm_file and sensor-emulator_odm_file.
claims.label: verified

claims.reason: odm.sensoremu.rc: vendor.sensoremu, user root, group root, disabled, oneshot, SYS_NICE, on-boot gate =sensoremu. odm.sensor-emulator.rc has the same shape with =sensor-emulator. odm_a/bin/sensoremu and odm_a/bin/sensor-emulator exist. vendor_file_contexts lines 129-130 map both binaries to hal_oculus_sensors_default_exec; lines 269 and 339 map the data directories to sensoremu_odm_file and sensor-emulator_odm_file.

claims.claim: The sensorlock HAL is an AIDL service registered as vendor.oculus.hardware.sensorlock.ISensorLock/default. It is paired with an AIDL NDK stub library (ISensorLock, ISensorLockListener), a libsensorlock.so backend that links libsmcihandler.so, and a /dev/sensorlock node. claims.claim: The system sensorservice daemon creates SensorService, starts the binder thread pool and registers with the default service manager. claims.reason: The odm manifest (vendor.oculus.hardware.sensors_java@1.0-service.xml) declares only IPowerstate. IPowerstateCallback appears in the library strings but is not a manifest interface. IPowerstate maps to hal_oculus_sensors_hwservice (vendor_hwservice_contexts line 49). The library is present in system_ext_a as 32-bit (86884 bytes) and 64-bit (124752 bytes) copies. The system_ext_a 64-bit copy has the same size as the odm_a copy but a different digest (640ed9df... vs 15f14589...), so the copies are not identical.
claims.corrected_claim: The odm sensors_java HAL (lib64, interface IPowerstate) is declared in the odm VINTF manifest with IPowerstate only; IPowerstateCallback appears in the library but is not a manifest interface. The IPowerstate descriptor maps to hal_oculus_sensors_hwservice. A library of the same name is present in system_ext_a in 32-bit and 64-bit builds; the 64-bit system_ext_a copy is the same size as the odm_a copy but has a different digest, so the copies are not byte-identical.

gaps: No disassembly or decompilation was performed. HIDL and AIDL method signatures, call graphs and runtime behaviour were not extracted; the only interface facts are descriptor strings and exported symbols.
All ELF binaries are stripped or lightly symbolised, so their roles beyond the imports and strings listed in the evidence are name-based (75 rows inferred).

Which HAL instance a shipping device runs is decided by a runtime property. Only odm_a/etc/build.prop was checked for the default (sensorservice). Other property sources such as persist data, /data overrides or vendor_a/build.prop were not searched for this key.

The interface lists disagree: the odm manifest declares 10 interfaces, the library has 40 vendor.oculus.hardware.sensors@1.0:: strings, and the SELinux hwservice contexts list 19 sensors entries. Which interfaces are registered at runtime was not determined.

SELinux policy was read only through grep of text .cil and *_contexts files. The precompiled_sepolicy binary under odm_a/etc/selinux and any policy binaries were not decoded, so the full allow set was not enumerated.
The 32-bit variants under system_a/lib and vendor_a/lib, and the 32-bit odm and product copies, were not inspected beyond their names and sizes.
meta.bin under system_ext_a/etc/bootanim (1081352 bytes) was not identified; its format remains unknown.

The TorchScript and PyTorch Lite archives were not decoded. Tensor shapes, input and output names, and the versioning semantics were not extracted. Producer metadata contains build host and user identifiers, which were deliberately not reproduced.

The exact TOML grammar and the device-version names used by sensorservice.cfg (kDeviceVersionName in libdeviceid) were not extracted, so the key-matching behaviour is only described from strings and comments.
sensor_validation (8.2 MB) and libsensorvalidation.so were classified from name, NEEDED list and the svt.sh invocation only; their internal test cases were not examined.
The four symlinks point to toybox and to boot vdex files outside this group; those targets were not analysed.

Libraries listed as dependencies of the sensors HAL and emulator but outside this group's rows (libsyncboss.so, libcamerahal.so, libclocksync.so, libwavreader.so, libgammacorrection.so, libcalibrationstore.so) were confirmed present but not inspected.
